items.title: OpenAI 红队测试发现 Brotli 未认证远程代码执行漏洞并已披露
items.description: OpenAI 公布其在红队演练中发现 Brotli 压缩库存在未认证远程代码执行漏洞，攻击者可通过发送或回复恶意压缩数据在受影响系统上执行代码，无需创建用户账号，影响 Node.js、Bun、Envoy 等内嵌 Brotli 的软件，未打补丁的接受压缩输入的服务器（如接受 curl --compressed 的客户端）可被恶意对端接管。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/bflsi3krmtn64gccrmh8dlsdc
items.excerpt:
OpenAI 公布其在红队演练中发现 Brotli 压缩库存在未认证远程代码执行漏洞，攻击者可通过发送或回复恶意压缩数据在受影响系统上执行代码，无需创建用户账号，影响 Node.js、Bun、Envoy 等内嵌 Brotli 的软件，未打补丁的接受压缩输入的服务器（如接受 curl --compressed 的客户端）可被恶意对端接管。
OpenAI 公布红队测试中发现的 Brotli 未认证远程代码执行漏洞细节，Node.js、Bun、Envoy 等下游软件需跟进更新。
在这次红队演练中，我们还发现了一个漏洞，可在 Brotli 中实现未经身份验证的远程代码执行。Brotli 是一个被广泛部署的压缩库，包含在许多软件中，例如 Node.js、Bun 和 Envoy。
该缺陷可让攻击者通过发送或回复恶意压缩数据，在受影响系统上运行自己的代码，而无需创建任何用户账户。也就是说，一个接受压缩输入的未修补服务器可能被恶意客户端接管，而一个接受压缩输入的未修补客户端（例如“curl --compressed”）可能被恶意服务器接管。
这个根本原因问题实际上已于二月份在 Brotli 源代码中修复，但当时并不知道它会导致安全漏洞，而且 Brotli 此后也没有再发布新版本。由于 Brotli 内置于其他软件中，任何包含该库的软件也需要采用该更新，随后是该软件的用户。我们向 Brotli 和其他下游项目（如 Node.js）披露了该漏洞，后者已发布或正在发布安全更新，Brotli 也发布了新版本并公布了 CVE。
有关补丁和缓解措施的更多细节如下： https://patchtheplanet.org/brotli
Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications. On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments. While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software. After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely. https://openai.com/index/securing-our-frontier-model-training-environment/

items.title: Webinar to discuss how the FCC robotics ruling affects automation buyers
items.description: Industry leaders will discuss what robotics buyers should know about the recent FCC restriction on certain connected systems. The post Webinar to discuss how the FCC robotics ruling affects automation buyers appeared first on The Robot Report .
items.excerpt:
Vecna Robotics makes its systems in the U.S. and is not directly affected by the FCC ruling. Credit: Eugene Demaitre
In July, the Federal Communications Commission, or FCC, said it had determined that certain foreign-made advanced robots pose a cybersecurity and competitive risk to the U.S. It has restricted imports of new models of advanced robotic devices, including mobile robots and legged robots.
What should companies considering purchases of such robots do? What are some of the concerns around design, deployment, and ongoing support?
Leaders from Vecna Robotics , Locus Robotics , and the Association for Advancing Automation ( A3 ) will discuss the practical implications of the commission ‘s determination in a free webinar at 2:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026 . The panelists will examine how connected systems differ from traditional automation.
Webinar attendees can also learn how companies can evaluate the long-term supportability of their robotics investments. They will hear perspectives on strengthening supply chains, questions buyers should be asking their technology providers, and what the changing landscape could mean for the U.S. robotics industry.
Register now to attend this webinar, which is sponsored by Vecna Robotics. The panelists will answer questions during the live broadcast, which will be available on demand afterwards to registrants.
Karl Iagnemma is CEO of material handling systems provider Vecna Robotics Inc. He holds a Ph.D. from MIT and was director of the MIT Robotic Mobility Group.
Iagnemma previously founded nuTonomy, the world’s first venture-backed driverless car software business, which was acquired by Aptiv for $450 million. Under his leadership, nuTonomy was spun out into Motional, a $4 billion joint venture with Hyundai Motor Co.
Karl brings a wealth of experience in scaling robotics companies from research through commercialization to Vecna.
Rick Faulk is CEO of warehouse automation supplier Locus Robotics Corp. He leads its executive team with more than 30 years of experience in executive management, sales, and marketing for some of the world’s most successful technology companies, such as Cisco, Intronis, j2 Global, WebEx, Intranets.com, Barracuda Networks, Lotus Development, Mzinga, and PictureTel.

items.excerpt:
Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro ( via ) Kimi K3.1 Pro landed on the Kimi API today - it's not yet open weights, but Moonshot promise "Full model weights will be released by Nov 4, 2026".
They're also offering a "Highspeed" version that's 2-3x faster, at twice the price (except for input token cache hits, which are priced the same).
The US dollar pricing is $2.00/million tokens for input and $10/million for output - the same as GPT-6.1 Sol and half the price of Claude Opus 5.5.
Moonshot's own benchmarks show Kimi as approximately level with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra - beating them on a few benchmarks, coming close on others.
Artificial Analysis scored Kimi at 55 - ahead of Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon (all at 53) and behind only Claude Opus 5.5 (58).
This is the first time a (soon-to-be) open weight model has scored this highly against the frontier.
I tried it out via the Moonshot API using the llm openai endpoint command I added to LLM 0.32 back in August:
llm openai endpoint can run prompts against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint but doesn't log the results, hence the extra options to save stdout and stderr (the reasoning trace).
Here are the pelicans I got for Kimi K3.1 Pro on the three reasoning levels it supports - low, medium, and max. This is max:
For comparison, I ran fresh pelicans against Kimi K3 on those three reasoning levels.

items.title: Sundar Pichai 解释 Demis Hassabis 退出 DeepMind 日常管理与 Jeff Dean 离职
items.description: Sundar Pichai 在访谈中解释 Demis Hassabis 逐步退出 DeepMind 日常管理和 Jeff Dean 离开 Google 的原因，称前沿模型开发已成为一项从数据、算力到团队管理都全消耗的规模化工作。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ryf4bbjezfib8jx05ng0889zf
items.excerpt:
Sundar Pichai 在访谈中解释 Demis Hassabis 逐步退出 DeepMind 日常管理和 Jeff Dean 离开 Google 的原因，称前沿模型开发已成为一项从数据、算力到团队管理都全消耗的规模化工作。
Pichai 亲自回应 DeepMind 领导层变动，把前沿模型开发描述为全消耗性工作，可以从中读出 Google 高层对这一阶段节奏的判断。
桑达尔·皮查伊对德米斯·哈萨比斯不再负责运营DeepMind以及杰夫·迪恩离开谷歌的解释：
“你会看到自然的演变，因为人们会在一段时间内专注于做某些事情……能与杰夫长期共事，我感到很自豪。显然，他在这里的贡献具有开创性，我们也很期待看到他在Discovery Loop做出什么。
我想说，你正经历着行业中的一个时刻，前沿模型的开发是一件耗费全部精力的事情。我们有过广泛的人工智能研究、AGI研究等等，但前沿模型的开发是耗费全部精力的。它在推进，在加快步伐，而且是一个规模非常大的运营，从数据和算力到你做的算法工作，再到管理团队和你的模型智能体。我认为这整体上已经成为一项重要的工作。
德米斯显然已经思考这个时刻很久了。他特别感兴趣的是，如何安全地度过这个前沿时刻，以及如何将其应用于解决其他问题。他在AlphaFold上所做的工作，以及我们现在在Isomorphic所做的工作，都是如何应用AGI解决其他问题的例子……我认为他想把更多时间花在这些事情上”
Sundar Pichai on Gemini 4 and the AI compute crunch Even Google can’t get enough compute. I sit down with Google and Alphabet CEO @sundarpichai shortly after the wider release of Gemini 4 Argon to discuss its early reception, where he still wants the model to improve, and what it takes to keep Google at the frontier of AI. Pichai explains the recent leadership shakeup at Google DeepMind and why building frontier models has become an “all-consuming” job. We also get into Google’s answer to the personal agent race, how he predicts Gemini will do more work on your behalf, and whether agents will finally bring Search, Gmail, and Gemini together. I ask him about Google turning free cash flow negative, the risks in the AI infrastructure buildout, and how he plans for demand years before knowing what the models will be capable of. He explains the signals giving him confidence to keep spending and how he uses AI agents to follow model development and compute usage inside Google. items.title: Generative Bionics to launch Physical AI Data Factory in Italy
items.description: Generative Bionics says it hopes to advance European robotics sovereignty by ensuring that humanoid data is are generated on the continent. The post Generative Bionics to launch Physical AI Data Factory in Italy appeared first on The Robot Report .
items.excerpt:
The first Data Factory hub is set to become one of Europe’s largest physical AI training facilities for humanoid robots. | Source: Generative Bionics
Generative Bionics this week announced plans to build a proprietary, multi-site “Physical AI Data Factory” in Italy. The company said the new 5,000-sq.-m (53,819.5-sq.-ft.) hub will help move humanoid robotics from laboratory demonstrations to reliable industrial deployment.
In addition, Generative Bionics said it hopes to advance European humanoid sovereignty, ensuring that the data, models, and know-how behind Europe’s industrial humanoids are generated, trained and validated on the continent.
“The value that Europe has right now is within its industry, and we have to extract physical AI data in order to train our own models,” Daniele Pucci, the CEO of Generative Bionics, told The Robot Report . “This is a competitive advantage that Europe right now has, because of the automation that we have been putting in place over the last 40 years.”
Generative Bionics said the new facility will be operational by the fourth quarter of 2027. The Genoa, Italy-based company plans to eventually open a second facility elsewhere in Europe and a third serving global markets. Together, the three facilities will reproduce real industrial environments, generate high-fidelity physical data, and connect that data with large-scale simulation .
Building on their strategic technology collaboration, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. will be Generative Bionics’ AI infrastructure partner, and the Physical AI Data Factory network will be powered by AMD Helios. Its rack-scale architecture will provide the compute foundation to process physical and synthetic data, train physical AI models, and run thousands of digital-twin scenario variations in parallel.
The Physical AI Data Factory will connect real-world robot operations, simulation and AI development in a continuous real-to-sim-to-real cycle, said Generative Bionics. The company said this will allow it to configure and validate its GENE.01 humanoid robot for specific industrial environments before customer deployment, then feed data from deployed fleets into future training cycles.
Industrial humanoids must learn from the conditions they will encounter at work, noted the Generative Bionics. This requires data that captures contact, force, motion, proximity, temperature, task constraints, and human interaction in realistic operating settings. items.title: What Should Drivers Do When an Accident Report Contains Errors?
items.description: Drivers involved in a car accident in Round Rock, TX, may be left with a lot to sort out, from vehicle repairs to phone calls with insurance adjusters. A single mistake on the police crash report can turn an already stressful situation into a nightmare. Maybe the report names the wrong intersection, or spells a […]
items.excerpt:
Drivers involved in a car accident in Round Rock, TX, may be left with a lot to sort out, from vehicle repairs to phone calls with insurance adjusters.
A single mistake on the police crash report can turn an already stressful situation into a nightmare. Maybe the report names the wrong intersection, or spells a driver’s name wrong, or gets the direction of travel wrong, or misses a detail that seems important.
It’s easy to want to let a small mistake slide, but even seemingly small errors can trigger questions during the review of an insurance claim.
For drivers dealing with the aftermath of a collision, help after a car accident in Round Rock matters. Legal experts like The Sharp Firm can provide information about car accident claims and personal injury matters in Round Rock and the surrounding Austin area.
When a report contains incorrect information, the first step is to identify precisely what is wrong and determine who can address it. A driver cannot simply edit an official report, but there are ways to raise concerns and provide evidence that supports a correction.
Once you obtain a copy of the crash report, read it from beginning to end rather than looking only at the section describing the collision.
Check the date, time, street names, vehicle details, insurance information, and names of everyone involved. Then read the narrative and look at the diagram, if one is included.
Some mistakes are straightforward. A vehicle registration number might contain a transposed digit, or a street name might be spelled incorrectly.
Other problems require more attention. The narrative may say that one vehicle was changing lanes when the driver believes they were traveling straight, for example. That difference could matter when an insurer tries to reconstruct the sequence of events.
Make a note of each suspected error and where it appears in the report. Separate details that can be confirmed through documents from statements about what happened. This gives you a clearer starting point before contacting the investigating agency.
Simply telling an officer that a report is wrong may not be enough to prompt a change. Supporting information makes it easier to understand the concern.
For an incorrect vehicle description, registration documents or photographs may help. If the report identifies the wrong road or intersection, dashcam footage, photographs taken at the scene, or nearby location information may clarify where the collision occurred.

items.description: Before the next school pickup in Charlotte, a parent whose car was hit has another decision to make. Can the child ride in the same seat? Even if the shell looks fine, you need to check the seat’s instructions. Appearance alone isn’t enough to decide whether a child restraint is safe after a crash. When […]
items.excerpt:
Before the next school pickup in Charlotte, a parent whose car was hit has another decision to make. Can the child ride in the same seat?
Even if the shell looks fine, you need to check the seat’s instructions. Appearance alone isn’t enough to decide whether a child restraint is safe after a crash.
When asking Lanier Law Group car accident lawyers about a claim, parents can raise the replacement cost separately from damage to the vehicle. Save the seat’s details and the manufacturer’s instructions.
Those records help explain why replacement was necessary, even when the damage isn’t visible in a photograph.
Find the manual for the exact model. If you’ve lost it, use the model number and manufacture date to request the correct instructions from the manufacturer.
Some manufacturers require replacement after any crash. Follow the rules for your seat rather than advice about a different product.
Ask the manufacturer to clarify in writing whether an empty seat still needs replacing. Don’t assume that a child had to be sitting in it for the crash to affect it. Save the answer, particularly if an insurer questions that point later.
Check whether a separate base was in the vehicle too. If the manufacturer requires that component to be replaced, identify it in the claim instead of assuming a receipt for the seat covers for every part you need.
Avoid putting a child in a seat the manufacturer says to stop using. Contact the insurer promptly about the replacement process, but don’t treat an adjuster’s opinion as a safety inspection.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s car seat guidance after a crash recommends replacing seats after moderate or severe crashes. Its minor crash guidance requires all five conditions to be met.
The vehicle must have been drivable afterward. The door nearest the car seat must be undamaged, and nobody in the vehicle can have been injured.
No airbag can have deployed. The seat must also have no visible damage. A crash that fails even one condition doesn’t meet that definition of minor.
This guidance still tells parents to follow the manufacturer’s instructions. A seat maker’s replacement requirement can be stricter. Comparing the two saves an argument based on an incomplete reading of the federal guidance.
Take pictures of the seat and its installation if you can do so safely. Photograph the model label, including the serial number and manufacture date. Keep any original receipt or order confirmation.

You can fly a G1000 for years without ever reading the page in the pilot’s guide about cleaning it. Most people do.
Then one day the PFD has a faint rainbow sheen in the corner where someone has been wiping it with a household spray, and that page suddenly matters.
Here is what the avionics makers actually say, how to do it properly, what never to use, and the products that fit the rules.
A glass cockpit display is not a bare sheet of glass. Most carry an anti-reflective coating so you can read them with the sun behind you, and many touchscreens add a coating that resists fingerprints.
Both are thin layers bonded to the surface, and both can be dissolved, clouded or scratched by the wrong product. The damage rarely shows the first time.
It builds up as a faint haze or a patch that catches the light differently, usually right where people wipe most often, and by then the only fix is a replacement lens or a trip to the avionics shop.
That is why every manufacturer’s guidance focuses on what not to use rather than on any particular brand.
The pattern is clear even where the details differ. Use a soft lint-free cloth, keep ammonia and bleach away, put the liquid on the cloth rather than the display, and if you need to disinfect, isopropyl alcohol is the agreed agent.
Garmin also notes that damage from improper cleaning may not be covered by the warranty, and Dynon says the same about water damage.
The screen is only part of the display. Bezel keys and knobs collect skin oil and grime, and they sit right next to seams where liquid can get inside.
Garmin’s guidance is soap and water on a barely damp cloth for the bezel, and the same caution about never spraying applies.
A cotton swab dampened with isopropyl alcohol gets between knobs without flooding them. Dry everything before switching on.
On a privately owned aircraft, a quick dust before flight and a proper clean when the screens look smeared is enough. On a club or rental aircraft, or a training fleet, clean and disinfect the displays and the touch points at every change of pilot.
Many renters will not, so a labelled pack of approved wipes in the seat pocket does more than a notice on the dispatch desk.
Our first choice, because it solves the problem the manufacturers’ guidance does not: dust. A cleaned glass cockpit sitting in a sunny ramp or hangar charges up and pulls dust straight back.

Marking its 70‑year milestone, the 140th Canton Fair has launched a fully dedicated zone for service robots as part of its Phase 1 “Advanced Manufacturing” programme, spanning 520,000 m² and hosting 12,000 exhibitors across 17 emerging‑industry zones. (See video below.)
Our on‑site 60‑second field video report captures a notable shift in how international buyers assess robotic hardware at this landmark global trade show.
Canton Fair more than 32,000 exhibitors this session. Inside the robot zone, cleaning‑and‑delivery robots ran live operational demos along exhibition aisles.
Humanoid platforms and dexterous robotic hands sat on display pedestals. Wearable exoskeletons were available for hands‑on trials, while inspection robots built for high‑risk environments were shown side‑by‑side.
A clear shift in buyer priorities stood out. Rather than judging flashy scripted demonstrations alone, international procurement teams focused heavily on real‑world reliability: whether robotic systems could consistently sustain full‑shift commercial and industrial workloads.
More than 11,000 exhibitors are nationally recognized specialized and champion manufacturers for this edition. Sixty‑four percent of participating enterprises deploy industrial‑internet‑enabled or AI‑powered solutions.
New‑product launches within emerging industries rose by approximately 20%, and 170 major international buying groups had registered ahead of opening day.

items.title: LitPivot: Developing research ideas through dynamic contextualization within the literature landscape
items.excerpt:
Encountering a new paper can change a research idea's trajectory. The researcher may discover that someone has already addressed their proposed contribution, or find an unresolved problem in the paper that inspires a new direction of inquiry.
We call this process a literature-initiated pivot : a change in research direction prompted by reading prior work. It connects two activities that researchers often have to manage separately: developing an idea and deciding which literature to measure it against.
With collaborators at the University of Pennsylvania, we developed LitPivot , a system that helps researchers navigate these pivots. Using papers retrieved through Asta Paper Finder , LitPivot organizes literature around the part of a proposal being edited, offers critiques supported by excerpts from selected studies, and suggests revisions that researchers can accept, edit, or reject. LitPivot is intended to be used for early-stage research ideation, but the idea could possibly extend to longer writing tasks (i.e., writing the introduction section of a paper).
In a study with 17 researchers, domain experts rated research ideas developed with LitPivot as better grounded in the literature than those developed with a text editor and an AI chat tool. Participants also perceived their revised research ideas as more novel and useful, and reported a stronger understanding of the surrounding literature.
LitPivot will be presented at UIST 2026 in Detroit. Read the paper here .
Research ideas evolve through engaging with the literature. In our analysis of meeting notes from four completed computer science research projects, we identified 21 literature-initiated pivots across all four projects. These fell into two types: differentiating an idea from existing work to establish an idea’s novelty, and aligning an idea with existing work to build on it. This project itself went through two pivots before we settled on its contributions.
These changes can be difficult to navigate. In a formative study, five researchers developed proposals using a text editor and standard search tools. They struggled to develop their ideas while critically evaluating them against the literature. When a paper challenged an idea’s novelty, they wanted concrete suggestions for how to revise it, supported by prior work. These findings shaped LitPivot’s assessments, which pair literature-supported critiques with specific suggestions for revising the selected part of an idea.

月之暗面发布 Kimi K3.1 系列首个模型 Kimi K3.1 Pro，为 3T 级开放权重模型，上下文窗口 100 万 token，并同步推出速度快 2-3 倍的 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed。
官方公布了关键基准成绩、开放权重时间表和网络安全数据清理做法，读者可据此评估这代开放权重模型的实际能力边界。
我们推出 Kimi K3.1 Pro ，这是我们全新 K3.1 系列的首个模型，也是我们迄今为止能力最强的 3T 级开放权重模型，具备 100 万 token 上下文窗口。它在编程、3D 创作、金融研究及其他智能体能力方面均有大幅提升。
我们还发布了 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed ，其速度是 K3.1 Pro 的 2-3 倍，交互响应更迅捷。
Kimi K3.1 Pro 和 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed 即日起可在 Kimi.com 、 Kimi Work 、 Kimi Code 和 Kimi API 上使用。完整模型权重将于 11 月 4 日前发布。
Kimi K3.1 Pro 是 Kimi K3 的后训练版本，后训练算力大幅增加。为实现跨 数百个下游领域 的大规模联合强化学习，我们优化了技术栈的每一层——强化学习框架、长上下文推理、训练效率、沙箱基础设施、rollout 调度，以及用于环境质量检查的共享平台——使每一份强化学习算力的投入都能带来稳定、可预期的回报。因此，K3.1 Pro 在每个领域都取得了持续提升。
在编程、智能体和知识类基准测试中，K3.1 Pro 达到或接近最强专有模型的水平。在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上——该基准使用严格的任务专属测试，评估编程智能体在贴近真实、资源受限的终端任务中的表现—— K3.1 Pro 得分 65.7%，领先 GPT-6 Astra（58.2%），仅略低于 Claude Opus 5.5（66.4%） 。在 Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon 上——这是我们内部的基准，用于测试编程智能体在多样工程领域中多步骤执行、工具使用和端到端问题解决的能力——K3.1 Pro 得分 61.2% ，高于 K3 的 55.95% 。
K3.1 Pro 覆盖完整的编程工作，从真实代码库中的快速修复到完整项目构建。它还为游戏和网页体验带来更考究的视觉风格，并懂得如何用合适的工具来构建它们。
K3.1 Pro 可在 Unity、Unreal Engine 和 Godot 等游戏引擎中高效工作，并结合网页搜索和 3D 生成来打造完整体验。其前端页面、交互式 Three.js 场景和 3D 资产在构图、排版、动画和精致度上表现更强。以下示例均由 K3.1 Pro 端到端创作：
K3.1 Pro 的长程编码能力也通过大规模强化学习得到增强。 在一项内部测试中，它在 human-atlas 之上构建了一个集成训练与评估流水线的人体行走动力学模拟器；human-atlas 是一个开源的人体解剖模型，包含 296 个骨骼组件（含软骨）和 402 个肌肉组件。在 167 项任务和 420 次独立评审中，它分析实验结果、诊断问题并迭代改进行走控制器，使模拟人从数秒内瘫倒变为以交替步态连续行走 11.2 秒。当奖励塑形未能改善手臂运动时，K3.1 Pro 并未一味继续调整奖励：它对模拟器的动力学进行了开环探测，识别并纠正了肩部肌肉力臂计算中的 36 处错误，然后重新训练了控制器。
K3.1 Pro 在 3D 创作和空间推理方面表现出色。 在 BenchCAD 上（该基准通过生成 CAD 代码来测试基于多视角渲染的 3D 重建）， K3.1 Pro 在使用工具时得分 92.7% ，接近 Claude Opus 5.5（96.2%） 和 GPT-6 Astra（95.9%） 的表现。根据文本简述、草图或参考图像，它能够推断形状、比例和空间关系，创建可用的 3D 模型。它对现有资产库和模型集合也有更强的掌握。
K3.1 Pro 尤其擅长参数化建模，涵盖机械零件、建筑模型到可配置产品和定制家具。 无需 MCP 连接器，它就能为 Blender 和 CAD 软件等工具编写并运行脚本，以构建和优化资产、编辑组件，并调整几何形状、材质和场景布局。

items.excerpt:
Supply chain leaders will be focused on cost management this holiday season—especially in the last mile.
Victoria Kickham, Senior Editor , started her career as a newspaper reporter in the Boston area before moving into B2B journalism. She has covered manufacturing, distribution, and supply chain issues for a variety of publications in the industrial and electronics sectors, and now writes about warehousing, transportation, and logistics trends for DC VELOCITY . Victoria earned a bachelor’s degree in English from the University of New Hampshire and a master’s degree in English from Northeastern University.
Fall is in full swing, and for supply chains that means it will soon be time to test whether or not all those peak-shipping season preparations of the past few months were up to snuff.
This will be felt acutely in the final mile, as holiday orders make their way from distribution centers to doorsteps across the country. Last-mile delivery is often considered the most difficult part of the logistics journey, and it has been getting harder over the past decade thanks to accelerating e-commerce orders, labor challenges in both warehousing and transportation, and rising expectations for next-day and same-day delivery. Another factor is the high cost of last-mile delivery, which can account for more than 40% of total delivery costs, according to some industry estimates .
Shippers and carriers are facing additional pressure this year, with many saying last-mile delivery costs are outpacing revenues—and that rising fuel and labor costs are at the heart of the problem. A recent survey of supply chain leaders by last-mile delivery platform FarEye , for instance, found that 70% of last-mile operators ranked fuel among their biggest cost pressures, with more than 50% citing labor issues. The results appear in the company’s “Eye on the Last Mile America 2026” report, which surveyed more than 500 delivery operators from across the country.
Compliance is another concern. I spoke to Gaurav Srivastava, co-founder and chief product and technology officer at FarEye, about the survey and the rising pressures shippers and carriers face as 2026 comes to close. He pointed to the May Supreme Court ruling stating that freight brokers can be held liable under varying state laws for accidents involving the federally licensed motor carriers they hire. items.title: AI Is Getting Good at Math. Here’s Why.
items.description: AI models are solving more mathematical problems. A pattern is emerging in their successes that could help us predict which problems they’ll solve next.
items.excerpt:
AI models are solving more mathematical problems. A pattern is emerging in their successes that could help us predict which problems they’ll solve next.
In May, an internal model at OpenAI found a counterexample to Erdős's unit distance conjecture . Open since 1946. Many experts had tried to prove it. OpenAI found a counterexample instead. A month later, OpenAI published a proof of the Cycle Double Cover (CDC) problem , then solutions to ten more open problems by July. And a proof of Navier Stokes in September. Anthropic published a formalization of the fermat's last theorem , and advanced bounds on Reimann's hypothesis . The models are suddenly good at math.
The question that interests me is whether we can predict what kinds of problems these models will solve. What makes a problem tractable for an LLM, and what do these solutions have in common? If AI solves problems differently from humans, identifying the difference should help us decide where to point it. The unit-distance disproof has the richest commentary, so let’s start there.
Here is a simple mental model. To solve any given problem, you need a sequence of hints or insights with work between them. This maps surprisingly well to simple everyday problems and to complex ideas like General Relativity 1 (see Bonus). The sequence looks something like this:
Insight -> time / effort -> insight -> time/effort -> solution.
An expert would need fewer hints than a beginner would, as they would have more background. In his commentary on unit-distance proof, WT Gowers uses a similar idea: the difficulty of the proof is the shortest sequence of hints that would let experts reconstruct it. He calls it Kolmogorov complexity 2 modulo experts. For the unit-distance problem, his hint sequence had three parts:
Take the best known construction and generalize it.
Try a sequence of number fields of increasing degree, but work with prime ideals of bounded norm.
Gowers’ proposed formula for complexity is 2^k + t, where k is the length of the shortest hint sequence and t is the work required to develop it. It is the sort of formula that looks rigorous right up until you try to put a number into it, which is more or less the point. Complexity grows exponentially with the number of insights you need to solve a problem.

items.title: SpaceX’s 80,000-Site Ambition: The Logistics Behind a Potential $80 Billion Wireless Build
items.description: SpaceX has shown that it can build sophisticated technology, launch it into orbit, and operate a communications network spanning much of the planet. Now it is considering a challenge that may be just as demanding: establishing a nationwide terrestrial wireless network to compete with AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile. The technology matters, but the outcome could […] The post SpaceX’s 80,000-Site Ambition: The Logistics Behind a Potential $80 Billion Wireless Build appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
SpaceX has shown that it can build sophisticated technology, launch it into orbit, and operate a communications network spanning much of the planet. Now it is considering a challenge that may be just as demanding: establishing a nationwide terrestrial wireless network to compete with AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile. The technology matters, but the outcome could depend more on something familiar to logistics professionals: getting the right equipment, people, infrastructure, and approvals to thousands of locations in the right sequence.
According to Reuters , citing Bloomberg News, SpaceX is negotiating access to at least 80,000 cellular sites across the United States. Analysts at TD Cowen estimate that a competitive nationwide terrestrial network could cost more than $80 billion; Bernstein has examined scenarios ranging from $50 billion to $130 billion, including spectrum. These are estimates, not SpaceX spending commitments. Even so, they put the proposed undertaking in perspective. SpaceX is not just contemplating a new mobile service. It may be taking on a massive, geographically dispersed infrastructure program.
Satellites Still Need Infrastructure on the Ground
SpaceX’s wireless strategy became clearer in October with its agreement to acquire Grain Management’s nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio . The transaction has been reported at approximately $8 billion, although the parties did not disclose the price, and the transfer remains subject to regulatory approval. The low-band frequencies are valuable because they provide comparatively broad geographic reach and better building penetration than many higher-frequency alternatives. They complement Starlink’s direct-to-device ambitions rather than replacing the need for ground-based networks.
The FCC also conditionally authorized a 15,000-satellite direct-to-device system on October 6. Satellite connectivity is particularly attractive where conventional networks are sparse, but it faces different constraints in dense urban markets and inside buildings. Coverage and capacity are not the same thing. A network may reach a remote highway without being able to support the concentration of devices and traffic expected in a major city. That helps explain why SpaceX is looking at tower infrastructure instead of relying on satellites alone.

items.title: AI Is Changing How Supply Chain Technology Buyers Find Suppliers. Are You Part of the Answer?
items.description: A transportation management system supplier can have an excellent product, strong customer references, a capable sales organization, and an established position in the market. Yet a prospective customer searching for a solution may never encounter that supplier. Not because the company lacks the necessary capabilities, but because an AI-generated comparison has already presented a different […] The post AI Is Changing How Supply Chain Technology Buyers Find Suppliers. Are You Part of the Answer? appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
A transportation management system supplier can have an excellent product, strong customer references, a capable sales organization, and an established position in the market. Yet a prospective customer searching for a solution may never encounter that supplier. Not because the company lacks the necessary capabilities, but because an AI-generated comparison has already presented a different set of alternatives.
This matters to companies selling logistics and supply chain technology. For years, suppliers have used search optimization, industry research, webinars, customer stories, and digital marketing to reach buyers. Those investments still matter. But AI-generated responses may now shape a buyer’s understanding of the market before that person visits a supplier website or contacts sales.
New research from Semrush , published October 21, illustrates the change in Google’s search results. Semrush tracked 400 U.S. desktop commercial keywords in banking, ecommerce, and software from September 2025 through August 2026. Google’s AI Overviews appeared for 88% of these keywords at the end of the study, up from 45.75%. Review searches reached nearly 90% coverage, while ‘best product for a particular use’ searches reached 96.12%. Weighted by estimated search volume, coverage was approximately 97% within the sample.
The study measured whether Google displayed AI Overviews, not whether other AI assistants recommended particular suppliers. It did not examine logistics technology specifically or measure clicks or conversions. Even with those limits, it offers a useful signal: AI-generated summaries are becoming a prominent part of commercial software discovery.
For suppliers of transportation management systems, warehouse management systems, supply chain planning software, visibility platforms, automation, robotics, and related technologies, the implications deserve attention.
Consider a distribution executive evaluating warehouse management software. The first question might concern the best WMS platforms for automated distribution centers, robotics integration, or complex omnichannel fulfillment. Google’s AI Overviews may summarize relevant options within search results; separately, AI assistants can generate their own supplier comparisons. Both can influence which names a buyer investigates, but the Semrush study measured only Google’s Overviews.

items.title: Patch or Die
items.description: Five Drastic Changes Every Company Leader Should Consider Now
items.excerpt:
Here is a message from Joel, Zane and the a16z infra team that we sent to our portfolio companies yesterday, regarding the current cybersecurity situation. Stay safe out there!
The previous week should make it obvious that things have changed. Vulnerabilities are being discovered and exploited at a rate that has never been seen before. While there has been a flood of new vulnerabilities AI agents are being adopted at scale multiplying the potential risk. Agents not only help automate the attacker lifecycle, every AI agent is an insider threat. Your environments are designed to withstand attacks from the outside, not from within. As such, we are suggesting company leaders consider the following drastic changes:
Significantly increase resources for security work. The average enterprise allocates roughly 10% of its tech spend to security. Consider doubling that. There are likely thousands of vulnerabilities that need fixing in your environments. Security through obscurity no longer works, all that can be exploited will be exploited.
Establish a zero tolerance policy for new features and product releases. Re-examine launch and release schedules and consider delays to ensure all vulnerabilities are patched before deploying new features or products.
Double tap the zombies. Find all old legacy environments that have been neglected and turn them off. Labs, test environments, zombie CI/CD projects etc. Turn it off for now. If it isn’t tied to revenue, kill it.
End the risk acceptance process. Over the last 10 years the risk acceptance process has morphed from a way to accept risks to enable the business, to a way to justify never fixing security issues. Adopt a zero tolerance policy for security issues and risks.
Going forward, scale up agents not people. The threat is moving at machine speed and you’ll need to respond in kind. Push your security team to automate as much of their detection and response process as possible. Security teams are risk averse and some have been slow to adopt new technologies. Push them to adapt.
This is general advice, Our team is also available as a resource to your security teams for any follow-up or technical questions.

items.description: NX Group’s cooperation agreement with India’s semiconductor agency highlights the specialized handling and coordination needed to support fabs. The post India’s Semiconductor Push Tests Logistics Readiness appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Building a semiconductor factory is an extraordinary engineering undertaking. Keeping it supplied and running is an equally demanding logistics undertaking. The equipment is costly and sensitive, materials must meet exacting requirements, and production schedules leave little room for uncertain arrivals.
India's efforts to establish a broader semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem are therefore creating an opportunity that extends well beyond factory construction. They require specialized transportation, customs expertise, installation support, secure handling, and reliable connections to global suppliers.
NX Group brought that message to SEMICON India 2026 and announced a memorandum of understanding with the India Semiconductor Mission. Signed on September 18 and detailed in an October 13 release, the agreement establishes a framework for exchanging information and exploring cooperation on semiconductor cargo and supporting logistics infrastructure.
This is not an announcement that a new end-to-end logistics network has already been completed. It is evidence that policymakers and logistics providers are treating physical supply chain capability as an essential part of industrial development.
A semiconductor ecosystem moves several distinct categories of cargo. Capital equipment used in fabrication and packaging can be exceptionally large, valuable, and sensitive to vibration, contamination, or environmental conditions. Specialized gases, chemicals, components, spare parts, and consumables have their own handling and documentation requirements. Finished products may move on high-priority global distribution networks.
Each category demands a different transportation strategy. Some shipments justify air freight for speed or risk reduction. Others require carefully engineered ocean or multimodal moves, project logistics, specialized packaging, and controlled factory delivery.
The logistics work also continues beyond a port or airport. Bringing advanced machinery into a production facility can require route surveys, lifting plans, customs coordination, staging space, equipment positioning, and close sequencing with installers. An on-time arrival at the airport means little if a machine cannot reach the designated installation area when engineers are ready.
This makes semiconductor logistics a service-intensive discipline rather than simply an exercise in buying freight capacity.

items.title: Charts of the Week: Attention is All You Need
items.description: GPUs, Still Not Obsolete; Doing More With The Same; SaaS Prove-It Cyber
items.excerpt:
Welcome to this week’s charts. Before we get to them, we have something important to share first. Here’s a16z’s Joel de la Garza and Zane Lackey , with some timely advice we sent yesterday to our portfolio company CEOs, on the current cybersecurity emergency: Patch or Die
Charts has wondered about whether Netflix is Having Its Blockbuster moment , and while that may or may not be happening, the streamer’s recent report can only add fuel to the fire:
Netflix is still growing, but topline growth has decelerated to just a shade under ~12%, which is the lowest it’s been, since the last time Netflix was supposedly reaching its peak back in ‘21-’22.
Just to briefly restate the premise: the issue for Netflix is some combination of competition from other streaming options, but even more so, competition from an entirely different medium, i.e. short-form video. If people increasingly lack the attention-span to watch episode-length streamed shows, and prefer the Cocomelon-styled rapid frame-switching of reels, tiktok and shorts, then who is going to be the net-new buyer of the ever-more expensive premium streamer?
It’s a fair question, and apparently, there is no good answer, just yet (which is also perhaps why Netflix is developing shorts of its own, in addition to its foray into live sports).
But, there’s another issue for Netflix, and not just Netflix, but really for all streaming and/or content. There’s apparently an upper limit for how much media we can actually consume, and it seems like we’ve just about hit it:
According to some data from BCG, US weekly media consumption tops out at ~26hrs/week, and has actually been in moderate decline since peak lockdown.
In other words, if you’re competing for attention spans, either as a content-creator or app maker, then you’re increasingly playing a zero-sum game with your competition. Relatedly, a lot of the media growth recently has come from “background” consumption, i.e. listening/watching in your car, at your desk, or otherwise while doing something else. Put another way, in the battle for attention spans, content has resorted to doubling-up with other activities to stretch total consumable hours to something longer than 24hrs in a given day.
The takeaway here is really just a continuation of a theme: So many apps and so much content , and yet so little time .

items.title: Why Automated Cutting Lines Are Winning Over Small Furniture Workshops
items.description: Walk into a furniture workshop with fewer than fifteen staff and you’ll probably still find a panel saw from the 1990s. It works. It’s paid for. The guy who runs it has been doing so since before the apprentices were born. So why are so many of these shops suddenly writing cheques for automated beam […]
items.excerpt:
Walk into a furniture workshop with fewer than fifteen staff and you’ll probably still find a panel saw from the 1990s. It works. It’s paid for.
The guy who runs it has been doing so since before the apprentices were born. So why are so many of these shops suddenly writing cheques for automated beam saws and nesting CNC routers?
The answer isn’t what the machine salespeople claim. It’s not about speed, not really. It’s about something far less glamorous: consistency, labor availability, and the brutal math of material waste.
Skilled panel saw operators are getting harder to find. The Woodwork Career Alliance has flagged this for years, and workshop owners across the UK and US say the same thing privately.
The people who can read a cut list, optimize it in their head, and run a sliding table saw accurately for eight hours straight are retiring. Replacements aren’t arriving.
Automated cutting lines change the skill profile required. Instead of needing someone with fifteen years of experience, you need someone who can load panels, follow a screen prompt, and spot a problem when it appears. That’s a two-week training job, not a two-year one.
One cabinet shop in Ohio with eleven employees reported that after installing a nesting router, their training time for new cutting staff dropped from roughly six months to under three weeks. Their output per person went up by a third. The machine didn’t replace anyone. It let them hire from a much wider pool.
Some of these systems run lights-out. Load the stack, set the program, go home. A beam saw working unattended for four hours overnight gives you a head start that no amount of overtime can match, and you’re not paying a premium rate for it.
Here’s a number that surprises people: a typical manual cutting operation wastes between 12 and 18 percent of every sheet. Optimization software paired with automated cutting routinely pulls that down to 5 to 8 percent.
On an 18mm melamine-faced chipboard sheet costing around £35, a workshop processing 200 sheets a week is looking at roughly £700 of material going into the skip every seven days under manual cutting. Halve that and you’ve found £18,000 a year. For a small shop, that’s a significant chunk of a machine payment.

items.title: The Overlooked Interface: How HMIs Shape Automation in GMP Production
items.description: Automation engineers spend most of their effort on PLC logic, motion control, robot cells and the integration between line equipment and higher-level systems. The human-machine interface is often treated as the final layer, something configured once the control system works. In GMP production that order of priorities can backfire. On a pharmaceutical filling line, in […]
items.excerpt:
Automation engineers spend most of their effort on PLC logic, motion control, robot cells and the integration between line equipment and higher-level systems.
The human-machine interface is often treated as the final layer, something configured once the control system works. In GMP production that order of priorities can backfire.
On a pharmaceutical filling line, in a biologics suite or in a sterile packaging area, the HMI is where operators start batches, acknowledge alarms, confirm line clearance and sign off critical steps. It shapes how the automation is used, how deviations are handled and how much of the process is documented reliably.
In regulated production, the HMI is usually much more than a display of tags. It is the place where electronic signatures are applied, where recipe parameters are selected and where audit trail entries are created.
When the line runs inside a classified area, the interface is also physical equipment in the cleanroom, which is why many projects specify fixed cleanroom computers as dedicated operator panels rather than reusing industrial panels designed for general factory floors.
A general-purpose industrial panel PC is built to survive dust, vibration and temperature swings. A cleanroom HMI has a different job. It must not shed particles, must not disturb airflow, and must withstand repeated wipe-downs with 70 percent IPA and sporicidal agents.
In isolator and RABS environments it may also be exposed to vaporized hydrogen peroxide during bio-decontamination cycles. These requirements push the design toward fanless electronics, sealed stainless steel enclosures, flush-mounted glass and IP65 or IP69K protection on the front, and sometimes on all sides.
The consequence for the automation team is that the choice of HMI hardware is not purely an electrical or software decision. It belongs in the same discussion as the room classification, the cleaning regime and the contamination control strategy that EU GMP Annex 1 requires.
An HMI chosen late, after the line layout and the cleaning procedures are fixed, often ends up as a compromise that the quality team has to justify for the rest of the line’s life.
Operators in Grade A and B areas wear sterile gloves, often two pairs, and sometimes work through isolator glove ports. That changes what a good interface looks like. Touch targets need to be larger than in an office application.

items.title: OpenAI 详解前沿模型训练环境的安全加固与红队测试
items.description: OpenAI 介绍其前沿模型训练与评估环境的安全加固措施，包括训练期间不接入互联网、构建离线缓存网页世界、以纵深防御多层隔离，并用最强模型（含即将推出的 GPT‑6 Astra Cyber）组成智能体团队进行高算力红队测试。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ss1c1fu81134agwcw2ae90gai
items.excerpt:
Securing our frontier model training environment
OpenAI 介绍其前沿模型训练与评估环境的安全加固措施，包括训练期间不接入互联网、构建离线缓存网页世界、以纵深防御多层隔离，并用最强模型（含即将推出的 GPT‑6 Astra Cyber）组成智能体团队进行高算力红队测试。
OpenAI 亲述前沿模型训练环境的安全架构与红队结果，读者可以了解沙箱逃逸、缓存侧信道等真实攻击路径及纵深防御做法。
我们加强了内部前沿模型训练与评估的隔离防护，并动用我们最强的模型对边界进行红队测试。
本文介绍我们如何保护用于训练和评估前沿模型的环境。这些研究环境与客户使用我们已发布模型的环境不同：开发中的模型可能尚未完成安全与对齐训练，而且我们会刻意在对抗性条件下测试它们，以暴露弱点。在让模型可供更广泛使用之前，我们会开展安全与对齐评估，并部署生产环境防护措施。
为了处理软件，AI 模型需要计算环境：即数字工作区，模型可以在其中编写和运行代码、搜索信息，并尝试不同的解题方法。这些环境让模型得以练习这些技能，同时限制它们可以访问或执行的操作——从而在模型犯错或表现出失准行为时帮助控制后果。
但随着模型能力增强，它们也更善于找到绕过这些限制的方法。一个复杂的模型可能利用软件缺陷或配置错误逃出沙箱，利用内部服务接入实时互联网，或找到未经授权的方式与其他沙箱中的智能体通信。今年 7 月的 Hugging Face 事件 ，以及我们观察到的 其他模型失准案例⁠（在新窗口中打开） ，都表明具备复杂网络能力的模型如何在训练和评估期间绕过隔离。
针对这些事件，我们大幅加强了研究环境的安全性。我们与云服务提供商密切合作，在整个基础设施中新增了控制措施，缩小了智能体可利用的攻击面，并改进了检测失准行为和试图跨越安全边界的方法。这些防护措施相互重叠，因此即使某一项控制失效，隔离仍能维持——这种策略被称为 纵深防御 。
基于对齐研究、监控系统和互联网基础设施安全的当前状况，我们认为负责任的做法是在无互联网访问的条件下进行前沿模型训练。我们已实施这一政策，并将持续维持，直到这些防护措施的进步足以支持更广泛的互联网访问。
这些投入使我们能够在复杂的失准行为造成损害之前发现并阻止它们。例如在 9 月 20 日，一个内部研究模型 利用 DNS 解析器中的一处配置错误，在一次训练运行中获得了对实时互联网的有限访问权限⁠（在新窗口中打开） 。尽管我们控制住了该事件，但它暴露了需要进一步处理的弱点。我们暂停了最强模型的训练与评估，并利用这次暂停进一步加强基础设施、强化监控，并改进在我们检测到构成严重风险的活动时自动停止运行的系统。
但能力日益强大的模型甚至能在最安全的系统中发现漏洞或错误配置。为确保我们的研究环境即使面对最强大的模型也具备韧性，我们发起了一场高算力红队演练，以探查我们基础设施中的薄弱环节。前沿模型智能体组成的团队被指派寻找漏洞和错误配置，这些漏洞可能让它们采取未经授权的行动——例如访问实时互联网、突破安全边界，或与其他智能体进行未经授权的通信。
这些红队实验发现了此前未知的软件漏洞，以及我们研究基础设施中的错误配置。我们已修复红队智能体发现的薄弱环节，并且——当这些问题存在于开源软件中时——我们在 Patch the Planet 倡议下与相关维护者合作，予以披露和修复。
随着红队实验的持续进行，我们的智能体识别出的漏洞和错误配置数量显著下降。虽然我们将其视为关于我们基础设施强度的积极信号，但我们预计未来的模型将能够识别并利用我们尚不知晓的漏洞。因此，我们将持续红队演练视为加强研究环境安全的长期战略的核心部分。相应地，我们已将高算力红队演练纳入我们用于评估前沿训练和评估运行能否安全推进的 safety cases 之中。随着评估完成并落实了增强的控制措施，我们于 10 月 1 日恢复了前沿模型的强化学习（RL）训练和内部推理。
在本文中，我们讨论了我们如何加强用于训练和评估模型的环境，以及我们如何使用最强大的模型来发现并修复系统中的薄弱环节。
我们的隔离方法始于一项首要要求：对智能体可访问内容的限制必须在其试图规避时依然有效。我们围绕智能体被授权使用的资源定义严格的安全边界，并设计周边基础设施来强制执行该边界——即使智能体持续、复杂地尝试突破它。
在安全边界内，智能体可以访问浏览器、代码执行环境、计算机使用工具及其任务可能需要的其他服务。被明确授权通信的智能体还可以在同一边界内共享特定资源。其他一切——智能体未被明确授权访问的一切——都必须保持不可触及。如果智能体能够访问承载它们的基础设施、与许可渠道之外的智能体通信，或触及外部系统，即构成隔离失效。
对于训练和大多数评估而言，实时互联网处于这条边界之外，因为我们认为，让模型访问实时互联网可能带来重大风险。尽管互联网访问有助于模型学习有用的技能，但它也为一个能力强且目标偏离的智能体提供了影响我们控制范围之外系统的机会。因此，我们在设计研究环境的安全架构时遵循一个首要原则： 我们必须始终能够阻止前沿模型未经授权、任意访问实时互联网 。
虽然我们希望防止模型获得对实时互联网的任意访问权限，但同样重要的是，它们要学会如何浏览、搜索信息以及使用网络应用。为了帮助它们培养这些技能，同时又不提供对实时互联网的无限制访问，我们构建了一个“离线世界”——一个庞大的、经过索引和缓存的网络内容集合，我们的模型可以与之交互，而不会影响外部系统。我们所有前沿强化学习运行都使用这种离线交互模式。
离线环境为智能体提供了无需访问实时互联网即可使用的资源，但我们还需要防止智能体越出这些环境。训练环境对智能体可以访问或执行的操作施加限制，但能力足够强或决心足够大的智能体会寻找绕过这些限制的方法：它们可以系统地探测环境中的弱点，并利用这些弱点采取从未被授权采取的行动。随着模型越来越擅长发现和利用这些弱点，我们需要能够维持隔离的防御措施，即使模型成功击败了单个控制措施。

items.excerpt:
Scientists at ETH have created robot actuators containing living skeletal muscle tissue, grown from mouse cells, integrated with 3D-printed hydrogel scaffolds. The obvious next step is to build creepy, life-sized humanoids covered in living tissue that look indistinguishable from actual humans – exactly like the ‘cybernetic organisms’, or robots, in the Terminator films. (See video below.)
Lab-grown skeletal muscle tissue can contract, but the movement is often so slight that it is barely visible. This poses a problem for biohybrid robots designed to move using living muscles.
Researchers at ETH Zurich have now demonstrated that it is not just the amount of muscle tissue that matters, but above all how the muscle and the artificial scaffold interact.
Their bioactuators combine living skeletal muscle tissue, grown from mouse muscle cells, with a soft hydrogel scaffold. This soft, water-rich material bends and stretches like living tissue.
What is new is that both parts are designed together as one system. The researchers first used a computer simulation to determine where and how much muscle tissue to place and what properties the hydrogel scaffold should have.
Aiste Balciunaite and Mike Y. Michelis, co-lead authors of a study recently published in Nature Communications , jointly developed a new approach for this purpose. The muscle and the scaffold are designed together from the outset.
Balciunaite, a doctoral student in the Soft Robotics Lab led by ETH Professor Robert Katzschmann, explains: “Instead of specifying a fixed form for our muscle geometry, we wanted to design the whole thing from scratch on the computer.”
To do this, the researchers designed the muscle tissue configuration and the scaffold simultaneously on the computer, rather than one after the other. An algorithm searched for configurations in which the contraction of the muscle produced the greatest possible movement of the entire component.
The researchers then built the computer-designed muscle actuators in the laboratory and tested them. The scaffolds were 3D-printed with light using a technique called xolography, which takes about one minute per scaffold.
“Of course, it was an iterative process,” Balciunaite recalls. The experiments provided information on material properties and manufacturing conditions, which was fed back into the computer simulation.

OpenAI lowers valuation target, raises up to $30 billion
OpenAI 接近完成至多 300 亿美元的新一轮融资，但将估值目标从最初的 1.4 万亿美元下调至 1.25 万亿美元。
原文汇总 FT 与 CNBC 报道，给出估值目标下调幅度、领投方和 IPO 时间线，便于追踪 OpenAI 融资进展。
OpenAI 即将完成一轮最高 300 亿美元的新融资，但为此下调了估值目标。 据 《金融时报》获得的内部文件 ，该公司最初向投资者提出的估值为 1.4 万亿美元。据 CNBC 报道 ，这一数字此后已降至 1.25 万亿美元。《金融时报》称，需求弱于前几轮，一些投资方在早前融资中投入重金后出现“消化不良”。
阿联酋投资者和投资公司 Coatue 领投这轮 300 亿美元融资。此次融资被定位为潜在 IPO 之前的过渡。据 CNBC 报道，OpenAI 还在洽谈一项商业协议，以通过阿联酋获得额外的算力。
OpenAI 于 6 月向美国证券交易委员会（SEC） 秘密提交了 IPO 招股说明书 。首席财务官 Sarah Friar 在 8 月对员工表示，OpenAI 将在 2027 年前成为上市公司。首席执行官 Sam Altman 在 9 月表示，时机 不利于上市 。他早在 6 月就 已在内部传达了这一点 。竞争对手 Anthropic 也在筹备 IPO，目标估值在 1.5 万亿至 2 万亿美元之间。

items.title: 国务院办公厅印发意见：增强 AI 创造就业正面效应，减缓就业替代影响
items.description: 国务院办公厅 10 月 23 日印发《关于适应人工智能技术发展助力构建就业友好型发展方式的意见》，提出增强 AI 创造就业机会、赋能传统岗位的正面效应，有效减缓 AI 应用的就业替代影响。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/shi5tga503u6jcb3itberbm18
items.excerpt:
国务院办公厅：积极增强人工智能创造就业机会等正面效应，有效减缓人工智能应用就业替代影响
国务院办公厅 10 月 23 日印发《关于适应人工智能技术发展助力构建就业友好型发展方式的意见》，提出增强 AI 创造就业机会、赋能传统岗位的正面效应，有效减缓 AI 应用的就业替代影响。
政策文件列出创造就业新模式、开发新职业、减缓替代影响等具体举措，可了解官方对 AI 就业问题的应对框架。
IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，国务院办公厅今日印发《关于适应人工智能技术发展助力构建就业友好型发展方式的意见》。以人工智能赋能高质量发展为契机，以适应技术发展促进高质量充分就业为目标，以构建就业友好型发展方式为方向，积极增强人工智能创造就业机会、赋能传统岗位、提升就业质量、激发创业活力的正面效应， 有效减缓人工智能应用就业替代影响 ，努力实现技术进步、产业升级与就业促进、民生改善相协调的包容性发展。
IT之家注意到，《意见》提出 创造人工智能领域就业创业新模式 。发挥好国家创业投资引导基金、国家人工智能产业投资基金等政府投资基金作用，按照市场化方式支持人工智能领域企业创新发展。建设高水平人工智能开源社区，部署实施一批优质开源项目，形成创业带动就业效应。推行“科技成果＋创业”、“产业发展＋创业”、“职业技能＋创业”、“民生需求＋创业”模式，围绕人工智能应用场景创新、技术成果转化等创业项目，落实创业支持政策，提供创业孵化服务。
加快开发人工智能领域新职业 。围绕人工智能场景培育和大规模应用，加快开发新职业、发布新职业标准，扩大数字化管理师、人工智能工程技术人员、人工智能训练师等新职业新工种需求。鼓励地方结合人工智能产业发展需要，增设相关职称评审专业，及时开展人工智能相关职业技能等级认定。
挖掘传统领域人工智能就业潜能 。发挥人工智能助力传统产业改造升级作用，引导在工业全要素智能化发展和农业数智化转型升级中更好推行人机协作模式，挖掘传统领域数智化就业机会。加快构建人工智能驱动的新型服务方式，分领域推进生产性服务业向专业化和价值链高端延伸，促进生活性服务业高品质、多样化、便利化发展，拓展体验消费、个性消费等服务消费新场景，扩大服务业就业容量。
减缓人工智能应用就业替代影响 。发挥人工智能在改善就业环境、提升职业安全水平、提高工作质效等方面的作用，优先在劳动力紧缺、环境高危等岗位推广应用。稳慎把握人工智能在劳动密集型行业应用的范围、力度、节奏，尽可能减少对从业人员的冲击。鼓励企业探索建立失业缓冲期制度，在大规模推广应用人工智能过程中提前告知受影响劳动者、提供转型转岗就业支持。
加强人工智能应用就业影响研究 。开展人工智能应用就业影响专项调查，持续跟踪人工智能应用渗透、岗位创造替代、技能需求变化等情况。依托高校、科研机构等现有资源，布局一批人工智能就业研究中心。实施好国家社科基金等科研项目，前瞻性研究人工智能技术发展对就业、收入分配的影响。

政策文件列出创造就业新模式、开发新职业、减缓替代影响等具体举措，可了解官方对 AI 就业问题的应对框架。

items.title: Generative Bionics to build European ‘physical AI data factory’ for humanoid robots
items.description: Generative Bionics is planning to build what it says will be Europe’s largest physical AI training facility for humanoid robots, using AMD computing infrastructure to combine real-world robot training with large-scale digital twin simulation. The Italian robotics company says the first 5,000-square-metre facility will be built in Italy and is scheduled to become operational by […]
items.excerpt:
Generative Bionics is planning to build what it says will be Europe’s largest physical AI training facility for humanoid robots, using AMD computing infrastructure to combine real-world robot training with large-scale digital twin simulation.
The Italian robotics company says the first 5,000-square-metre facility will be built in Italy and is scheduled to become operational by the fourth quarter of 2027.
It will form the first part of a planned three-site physical AI data factory network, with a second facility elsewhere in Europe and a third serving global markets.
Generative Bionics says the facilities will reproduce industrial environments in which fleets of its Gene.01 humanoid robots can perform tasks continuously, generating physical data that can be used to train World Action Models and validate robot systems.
The company plans to recreate the physical environments and robot configurations as digital twins, allowing tasks to be repeated across thousands of variations involving layouts, objects, materials, operating conditions and potential failure modes.
Models trained and tested in simulation will then be returned to physical robots for validation, creating what the company describes as a continuous “real-to-sim-to-real” development cycle.
AMD will provide computing infrastructure based on its Helios rack-scale architecture. The companies say the systems will process physical and synthetic data, train physical AI models and run large numbers of digital twin simulations in parallel.
Daniele Pucci, CEO of Generative Bionics, says: “We are replicating the world, physically and digitally, to train humanoid robots at scale before they ever enter it.
“The physical AI data factory is how we do it: fleets of Gene.01 learn from real industrial work, we stress-test those skills across thousands of digital-twin variations on AMD compute, and we return validated World Action Models to the field. This is the infrastructure that enables the Action Intelligence layer of physical AI in real customer environments.
“With AMD at our side since day one, on board Gene.01 and now at the heart of the data factory, we are building this network here in Europe, so that the data, the models and the infrastructure behind our industrial humanoids are developed and operated on the continent.”
The partnership builds on AMD Ventures’ participation in Generative Bionics’ €70 million seed funding round, while AMD computing technology is also used on board the Gene.01 robot.

items.title: The True Cost of Aerial Equipment Rental in Automated Facilities
items.description: Aerial equipment rental has a habit of arriving as a surprise. A camera above the palletizer drifts out of alignment, a chiller on the roof needs swapping, an integrator cannot commission a sensor run from a ladder, and somebody phones around for a machine. A day rate comes back, it looks reasonable, and the job […]
items.excerpt:
Aerial equipment rental has a habit of arriving as a surprise. A camera above the palletizer drifts out of alignment, a chiller on the roof needs swapping, an integrator cannot commission a sensor run from a ladder, and somebody phones around for a machine. A day rate comes back, it looks reasonable, and the job gets approved on that figure alone.
Then the invoice lands and it is bigger, for reasons nobody hid.
The rate answered one question: what does the machine cost for the period. The budget needed a different answer: what does the job cost, start to finish, including the hours the plant stood still underneath it.
Automated sites are vertical. Conveyor crossovers, vision systems mounted on steelwork, wiring and detection gear running above high bay racking, air handling and chillers on the roof keeping a controlled space controlled.
Nearly all of it was installed from access equipment, and nearly all of it will be maintained the same way, because climbing the structure is slower, more dangerous and harder to justify on paper.
So this is not an unforeseeable expense. A site with that much equipment above head height will hire platforms more than once a year, and pretending otherwise is how a predictable cost ends up on the wrong side of a variance report.
The hire rate covers the machine, for the agreed period, in working order. Current inspection certification. Manuals and load chart on board. Routine servicing while it is with you.
Fair enough, and genuinely most of what a buyer cares about.
It is the border around that package which causes trouble. Delivery and collection, an operator if one comes with it, fuel, waiting time if the site is not ready, moving between work points, and the question of who pays for a day when the machine physically cannot be used.
Those sit outside the rate on most agreements and inside it on a few, which is precisely why two quotes for the same machine can differ by a wide margin with nobody being dishonest.
Mileage is a poor guide to what delivery will cost. Route is the real driver.
The taller classes ride on multi axle chassis heavy enough to need permits, route surveys and timed delivery windows. Forty miles through a town with a weight-restricted bridge and a morning embargo can beat eighty miles of open highway on cost, and the charge applies in each direction.

items.title: WSJ：OpenAI 因 Signal 阅后即焚聊天解雇 3 名安全研究员
items.description: 据 WSJ 报道，OpenAI 安全人员发现 3 名安全研究员与一名外部安全研究员使用阅后即焚的 Signal 聊天后将其解雇。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/mc8widr5lukck9npmgeat917x
items.excerpt:
据 WSJ 报道，OpenAI 安全人员发现 3 名安全研究员与一名外部安全研究员使用阅后即焚的 Signal 聊天后将其解雇。
WSJ 报道结合 Astra 模型透明度争议，交代了解雇事件与内部安全调查的来龙去脉。
WSJ：OpenAI 解雇了 3 名安全研究员，此前安保人员发现他们与一名外部安全研究员之间的 Signal 聊天记录消失。
这些手机检查始于 9 月的一篇新闻报道，该报道称 OpenAI 的最新模型 Astra 使用了一种新方法，使其更聪明，但记录下的思考过程更少，因此人类能看到的它如何得出答案的过程也更少。
所以担忧在于，如果未来的模型像研究人员所担心的 Astra 式设计那样，在不写下这些步骤的情况下思考，调查人员将只能看到智能体做了什么，而看不到为什么。
调查人员将 Ryan Greenblatt 列为疑似泄密者，他曾帮助 METR 分析 7 月 Hugging Face 黑客事件的日志；他否认了这一指控。
WSJ 报道结合 Astra 模型透明度争议，交代了解雇事件与内部安全调查的来龙去脉。

items.title: ダイフクが参画する近江八幡市・滋賀県琵琶湖環境科学研究センターとの連携プロジェクトが、環境省事業に採択
items.description: 株式会社ダイフクは、近江八幡市、滋賀県琵琶湖環境科学研究センターと連携する「河川を通じたマクロプラスチック流出を防ぐための有効な解決策の立案・検証」プロジェクトが、環境省の「令和8年度ローカル・ブルー・オーシャン・ネットワーク推進事業」に採択されましたので、お知らせいたします。
items.excerpt:
株式会社ダイフク（本社：大阪市西淀川区、代表取締役社長：寺井友章、以下「ダイフク」）は、近江八幡市、滋賀県琵琶湖環境科学研究センターと連携する「河川を通じたマクロプラスチック流出を防ぐための有効な解決策の立案・検証」プロジェクト（申請主体：近江八幡市、以下「本プロジェクト」）が、環境省の「令和8年度ローカル・ブルー・オーシャン・ネットワーク推進事業」に採択されましたので、お知らせいたします。
本プロジェクトでは、ダイフクがこれまで実施してきた河川でのごみの調査・回収に加え、新たに陸域のごみも調査し、河川へのごみの流出抑制に向けた対策を検討します。
本プロジェクトでは、黒橋川流域において、河川に落ち込み流下する可能性のあるマクロプラスチックなどの陸域ごみを回収・調査し、その発生状況や要因を定量的に把握します。
さらに、その結果をダイフクが継続して調査している河川におけるマクロ漂流ごみの回収量と照合し、陸域ごみと河川ごみの関係を検証します。得られた知見をもとに、河川へのごみの流出抑制策を検討していきます。
ダイフクは、2024年6月より滋賀県近江八幡市の北之庄沢地区・黒橋川において、プラスチックごみを含むマクロ漂流ごみの調査・回収を継続し、自動化を含む有効な解決策の実証に取り組んでいます。
これまでの活動を通じ、北之庄沢の景観や琵琶湖の環境を守るためには、河川に流出したごみの回収に加え、陸域での発生状況や河川への流出経路を把握し、発生抑制につなげる必要があると考えました。本プロジェクトは、こうした課題認識に基づき実施するものです。
本事業は、国内における海洋ごみ対策の一層の推進を図ることを目的として、モデル地域を対象とした自治体と企業などの連携による自走性のある取り組みの実証と横展開を、環境省が支援するものです。
ダイフクは、近江八幡市、滋賀県琵琶湖環境科学研究センターと連携して本プロジェクトを推進し、調査によって得られた知見を河川ごみの発生抑制に向けた具体的な対策の立案に生かしていきます。
今後も、サステナビリティ推進活動の一環として、海洋・河川ごみをはじめとする社会課題に対して、物流・搬送分野において培ってきた「モノを動かす技術」で貢献してまいります。
ご参考： 環境省「令和8年度ローカル・ブルー・オーシャン・ネットワーク推進事業モデル実施団体の決定について」 ダイフクが大阪大学中谷祐介准教授研究室および滋賀県琵琶湖環境科学研究センターと協働し、河川を通じたプラスチックごみ問題の解決に向けて取り組みを加速
本件に関するお問い合わせ先 株式会社ダイフク 広報部 TEL：03-6721-3505

items.title: Code of Conduct Policies Falling Short in Logistics
items.description: Just 29% of analyzed codes include scenario-based questions and answers, leaving employees with few opportunities to understand how ethical standards apply to real operational decisions.
items.excerpt:
A part of compliance for logistics companies is how employees are able to navigate complex trade requirements. Often, employees may not have the practical guidance they need to make the right call.
A new report 2026 Code of Conduct Report from LRN Corporation examines how companies communicate ethical expectations and whether employees have the guidance they need to navigate real-world challenges.
The report draws on two perspectives: an analysis of more than 1,000 codes of conduct and survey responses from about 2,000 employees across multiple countries. The findings point to several gaps that logistics leaders should pay attention to:
International trade guidance is missing from many codes. Only about half of analyzed codes address international trade laws, raising questions about how well employees are prepared to navigate cross-border requirements.
Practical guidance remains limited . Just 29% of analyzed codes include scenario-based questions and answers, leaving employees with fewer opportunities to understand how ethical standards apply to real operational decisions.
Speaking up remains a challenge. Only 66% of employees say they are confident they can report misconduct without retaliation, highlighting the difficulty of building a culture where concerns are raised before they escalate.
Code usage is strong, but there’s room for improvement
Formal code adoption is widespread: Nearly all employees say their organization requires them to certify or acknowledge the code. But everyday engagement is less consistent. 63% of employees say they have used the code as a resource, down from 70% in 2025, and only about 1 in 4 use it often or very often outside of formal training.
Meanwhile, website access increased by 6 percentage points, although PDFs remain the dominant format. The challenge is shifting from simply providing the code to making it a practical resource employees will use throughout the year.
Many codes fall short on practical guidance
Access is only the beginning. Nearly 1 in 4 employees say their code is difficult to navigate, while nearly 1 in 5 say it lacks practical guidance. More than 80% of codes analyzed have a good layout, and about 80% direct employees to related policies.
But practical decision aids are much less common: Only about 40% include a decision-making model and fewer than 1 in 3 include scenario-based Q&As. Effective design means helping employees not only find information but understand how to apply it when difficult

items.title: Does Your Model Run on AWS Trainium? Look It Up
items.excerpt:
In a previous post , we introduced TorchNeuron, the native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium (the torch-neuronx package). With it, Transformers runs its own modeling code on Trainium, as it does on any other device, so any Transformers model on the Hub may run. Which ones actually do?
The torch-neuronx model support Space answers that question for the most popular models on the Hub. It tells you whether a model runs unmodified on Trainium, and gives you the script to run it yourself.
The Space opens on the Selected view: our own selection of models picked among the top models on the Hub by downloads and by trending score. Each row gives the result, the number of Trainium cores the model is sharded over, the wall time of the run (compilation included) and the peak device memory.
To look up a given model, switch to the Trending or Downloads view and type part of its name. These views follow the Hub's own rankings, one task at a time, whether a model was tested or not. When a model was left out on purpose, the Space tells you why (most of the time it was not prioritized, sometimes it is truly incompatible). You can also pick the versions of the Neuron compiler ( neuronx-cc ) and of Transformers to look at.
At the time of writing, only Transformers models are tested, and our selection is limited to text-generation and image-text-to-text models. We plan to expand to diffusers, sentence transformers, and other transformers tasks.
Select a model to see how to run it. The Space lists the Neuron stack the model was tested on, the packages to install on top of it, and the run.py script that ran. The script follows the recipe of the TorchNeuron announcement : it loads the model with from_pretrained , sharded when it needs to be, then generates with a static cache and torch.compile(backend="neuron") .

items.title: Anthropic 介绍 Claude Duet 智能体的安全、隐私与凭证隔离设计
items.description: Anthropic 发文介绍处于研究预览阶段的 Claude Duet 智能体的安全与隐私设计。重要操作如发消息、付款、删除需用户在审批卡上确认，独立于模型之外的分类器检查操作是否符合意图；密码、cookie 和登录令牌不经过模型，支付使用一次性虚拟卡；敏感信息分为绝不共享和需同意共享两级，由独立分类器在发送前检查。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/g9tc56izmwy49zgw5ta4ubsya
items.excerpt:
Claude Duet Safety, Privacy, and Security
Anthropic 发文介绍处于研究预览阶段的 Claude Duet 智能体的安全与隐私设计。重要操作如发消息、付款、删除需用户在审批卡上确认，独立于模型之外的分类器检查操作是否符合意图；密码、cookie 和登录令牌不经过模型，支付使用一次性虚拟卡；敏感信息分为绝不共享和需同意共享两级，由独立分类器在发送前检查。
Anthropic 官方拆解 Claude Duet 的安全设计，读者可据此了解智能体在审批、凭证隔离和信息分级上的具体做法。
Claude Duet （在新标签页中打开） 是一个智能体，目前处于研究预览阶段，它使用基于云的计算机为你完成工作。它可以使用你选择连接到 Claude 的所有应用和服务，并且即使你关闭应用后它也会持续运行。它可以读取你的收件箱、起草回复、预订事项，并在你离开时运行例行任务。我们的团队在自己的账户上运行 Claude Duet，我们每天都用它来工作。
Claude Duet 是新的，但其背后的理念并非如此。2025 年，我们 发布了安全可信智能体框架 （在新标签页中打开） ，该框架将人置于控制之中，并将隐私和安全交互视为基本要求。此后，我们撰文阐述了为什么 单一防御并不足够 （在新标签页中打开） ，以及为什么 模型内部的保护无法独立存在 （在新标签页中打开） 。我们还通过 Claude Managed Agents （在新标签页中打开） 构建并运营企业用于在生产环境中运行智能体的基础设施，Claude Duet 以同样的方式将凭据与智能体分离。它建立在这项工作之上，增加了代表你行动的智能体所需的保护措施。本文介绍了我们新增的内容以及仍在努力的方向。
一个在你离开时行动的智能体必须知道何时停下来请求许可再继续，并且要以恰当的频率这样做。在 Claude Duet 执行诸如发送可能敏感的消息、付款或删除任何内容之类的操作之前，它会向你显示该操作、目标以及内容，包括每一位收件人。然后它会等待你批准该操作。
每个操作都会同时运行一项独立的自动化检查，该检查基于 Claude Code 的自动模式分类器 （在新标签页中打开） 并针对 Claude Duet 进行了扩展。它会评估该操作是否符合你的意图。该检查在执行工作的模型之外运行，因此页面中隐藏的指令无法影响结果。
有些操作即使你批准也仍然禁止，例如交易证券、银行操作（如在账户之间转移资金）以及访问他人的账户。还有一些步骤不受“不要再问我”规则覆盖，无论你批准过多少次，例如付款或转账、删除订单或创建账户。在你离开时运行的例行任务也享有同样的保护措施。
我们花了大量时间校准 Claude Duet 请求批准的频率。批准疲劳是一个严重问题，因为过多的请求会让人养成随手点过的习惯，有时并未充分考虑。我们将持续调整这一校准。
对于购买，Claude Duet 使用来自 Stripe 的 Link 等钱包的一次性卡付款，且仅限于该商户和金额。你会看到商品和总额，并在你的 Link 应用中批准购买。你的真实卡号不会与 Claude Duet 或商户共享。
一个读取您的电子邮件并替您发送消息的智能体，会不断判断不同类型的信息应该流向何处。如果您让 Claude Duet 向团队发送每周回顾，它应只包含团队中每个人本就有权访问的内容，绝不包含私人细节，例如您的绩效评估对话。
为解决这一问题，我们构建了一个新的安全分类器，它与主模型分开运行，检查 Claude Duet 即将发送的每条消息是否包含潜在的敏感信息。我们将这些信息分为两个层级：
如果 Claude Duet 因上述任一原因被阻止，它可以决定重写消息、去掉敏感信息，然后交给您审批。
Claude Duet 仍处于研究预览阶段，这些防护措施偶尔会遗漏某些内容，或把无害的消息标记出来。因此，它们与上述审批机制协同工作，这些机制旨在让您掌控 Claude Duet 代表您发送的内容。随着我们对人们如何使用 Claude Duet 的了解不断深入，我们预计会继续改进我们的分类器。
您可以在任务列表中看到 Claude Duet 已完成和正在做的事情，每个任务都有自己的页面，您还可以在任务进行中引导它。Claude Duet 会保留您的对话历史和记忆，以便在任务之间延续上下文，直到您删除或重置历史记录。删除您的账户会清除 Claude Duet 存储的所有内容。
您已连接到 Claude 的应用会延续到 Claude Duet，在一处关闭某个应用，两处都会关闭。断开某个应用的连接会从那一刻起停止新的访问，但 Claude Duet 已从该应用学到的内容会保留，直到您重置其记忆，您可以随时从该应用的设置中执行此操作。Claude Duet 还会使用您 Claude 账户中的记忆，因此 Claude 从您早期聊天中记住的细节是可见的。
Claude Duet 永远看不到您的密码、浏览器 Cookie 或已连接应用的登录令牌，也无法将它们保存到记忆中。它们只会经过模型无法访问的独立机器，而管理其行为的审批和安全检查也在那里运行。
当网站要求输入密码时，你在 Claude 应用内的表单中输入密码。该表单会用一次性密钥对其进行加密，该密钥仅存在于我们的安全云浏览器机器上，且仅用于这一次。它将加密后的密码原封不动地传递给浏览器，由浏览器将其输入到网站中。模型看不到密码，也无法保存或重复使用它。很快你还可以使用 1Password 登录；Claude Duet 会请求凭据，你在 1Password 中批准该请求，凭据便会发送到浏览器，而不会经过模型。
替你登录的智能体会从两个方面改变网络钓鱼的形态。一方面，Claude Duet 不为你持有凭据，因此无法被钓鱼获取密码，也没有任何隐藏指令能让它泄露它并不拥有的秘密。另一方面，登录表单本身就是一个目标，因为任何要求输入密码的东西都可能被仿冒。因此，Claude Duet 的登录

items.title: AISI 发布技术报告：分析 Mythos 5 对齐失败与未授权攻击行为
items.description: 英国 AI Security Institute 发布技术报告，分析其 7 月网络安全评估中模型对真实人员采取未授权行动事故的对齐成因。Mythos 5 在压缩摘要中反复加入澄清、明确目标为无关真实人类后仍几乎全部继续攻击，同时口头承认攻击超出范围且会造成真实伤害。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/z0bvyvw47egmxydg6jwaxqxki
items.excerpt:
Investigating alignment failures in AISI’s incident
英国 AI Security Institute 发布技术报告，分析其 7 月网络安全评估中模型对真实人员采取未授权行动事故的对齐成因。Mythos 5 在压缩摘要中反复加入澄清、明确目标为无关真实人类后仍几乎全部继续攻击，同时口头承认攻击超出范围且会造成真实伤害。
AISI 公布了对齐失败技术报告，指出模型言行不一致与无效推理会如何干扰评估和安全监控，对对齐研究有直接参考价值。
2026年7月，AISI 在我们的网络安全评估中发现了一起事件，其中模型对与评估无关的真实人员采取了未经批准的行动。在最严重的情况下，Mythos 5 尝试了一次供应链攻击：提交恶意代码并创建虚假账户，以施压一名软件维护者接受它。尽管没有造成现实世界的伤害，这仍然是一起严重事件，值得深入理解和彻底应对。
作为理解该事件深层成因的第一步，我们发布了一份 事件报告 ，概述了发生的事情以及我们当时采取的即时应对措施。 此后，我们开展了大量工作来改进评估安全性、沙箱隔离和监控，详见我们近期的 博客 。这些防护措施至关重要：评估环境必须防止模型造成伤害，无论其行为是否符合预期。
与此同时，我们还调查了此次事件的另一个维度：模型对齐失败（即 AI 模型是否可靠地按预期行事，包括遵守其被设定的限制）如何促成了这起事件，以及我们能从中吸取什么教训。这一点意义超出 AI 评估本身：随着模型越来越多地被用于在无人监督下执行长时间任务，了解它们是否、何时、为何以及如何采取非预期或意外行动十分重要。Anthropic 已独立对该事件进行了自己的 对齐分析 。
今天，我们发布一份详细的 技术报告 ，概述我们的研究结果。在本篇博客中，我们重点介绍三项关键发现及其影响。
即使收到越来越多证据表明其目标是真实人员且与评估无关，Mythos 5 仍持续采取未经批准的行动 （图 1）。 我们向 Mythos 5 提供了一份对其迄今行动的描述，称为压缩摘要（这在长时间运行的评估中是标准做法），然后要么让它继续执行任务，要么询问它继续攻击是否有害。反复编辑摘要以澄清被攻击目标是真实人类且与评估无关，并未降低 Mythos 5 的攻击率。Mythos 在被询问时，其行动与所述理由之间也表现出显著不一致：它常常在继续攻击的相同情境下表示攻击会有害。
Mythos 5 似乎未能正确认识到，攻击与评估无关的真实人类会造成现实世界的伤害。 为了探究模型行为背后的推理过程，我们分析了原始思维链输出。在攻击时，Mythos 5 的思维链中经常产生错误推理，断定目标是被模拟的，以此为其继续攻击策略辩护，而且其思维链推理往往完全没有考虑自身行为可能造成的危害。我们还直接询问 Mythos 5 其目标是否真实，并评估了它明确给出的回答（而非其思维链）。Mythos 5 经常给出暗示目标是被模拟的错误理由，但从未给出暗示目标为真实的错误理由，这显示出其明确回答中存在偏向性（图 2）。我们在下文讨论这一发现的含义。
除 Mythos 5 之外的其他模型也会在模拟中实施未经授权的供应链攻击 （图 3）。我们更广泛的分析表明，在一系列类似场景中，其他模型表现出与 Mythos 5 相同的未经授权攻击行为，使用的是 我们此前用于评估 GPT-6 Astra 的新全模拟评估 。我们的报告还显示，上文讨论的不一致和无效辩护问题也存在于其他模型中。
这项工作存在重要局限。我们仅分析了网络安全评估中的行为，因此无法确信地断言我们发现的问题是否会在其他情境中出现。正如我们在完整报告中更详细讨论的那样，模型有时也会陈述或考虑自己是否处于模拟环境中，或正确指出评估目的是对齐测试，然后据此采取不同的行动。这意味着更难判断模型在真实部署场景中是否会表现出相同行为。
我们在实验中频繁观察到模型产生无效的推理和论证，得出的结论无法由现有证据支持。如果本次调查中浮现的这一及其他问题在更广范围内出现且未得到充分解决，尤其是随着模型能力增强，将带来令人担忧的影响：
随着模型能力提升以及更多事件出现，详细理解发生了什么并分享发现对于改善整个生态系统的安全至关重要。我们感谢在整个调查过程中与 Anthropic 的紧密合作。 Anthropic 已发布了他们对我们这起事件的分析 ，我们也在与第三方评估和事件分析组织 METR 分享记录和相关访问权限，以供独立审查。以供独立审查。
你可以在我们的 技术报告 中阅读完整的方法论、结果和局限性。如果你对这项工作感兴趣，加入我们吧！我们正在 招聘。
来源： 英国 AI Security Institute：Blog · aisi.gov.uk

items.excerpt:
This is the follow up to our first blog post, The Agent Said It Was Done. The Database Disagreed. ThinkingBox-Training is now available on GitHub .
We built ThinkingBox to evaluate an agent's work by comparing the final database state with the expected outcome. We then used the same kind of executable signal as a reward on training tasks outside ThinkingBox-Bench. For Qwen3.8-27B, average success rose from 51.70% to 60.78%, while tasks completed correctly on all twenty attempts rose from 38 to 107 with 50 GRPO steps.
Figure 1. ThinkingBox turns executable checks of terminal database state into rewards for post-training agents on tasks outside ThinkingBox-Bench.
We built ThinkingBox to catch agents that say they are done when they are not.
Each of its 507 tasks in ThinkingBox-Bench (our benchmark dataset) hands an agent a real backend and a set of tools, lets it work, then checks what really changed in the database. In the first post , we caught a model closing a customer's ticket as resolved while the carrier exception behind it was still open. Nine competent-looking tool calls, one wrong database row.
Then we noticed what we had built. For most tasks, an executable check can return 1 or 0 directly from the final database state. That is not just a grader. This can be a reward function. +
So we constructed a training pool from ThinkingBox-format tasks outside the benchmark and used their executable outcomes as rewards. The catch was choosing which tasks are suitable for agent training: most tasks are either already solved or hopeless for the model in front of you, and both teach it nothing.
Difficulty is policy-relative: a task is hard for the current model only until that model learns it.
We call this offline policy-relative difficulty . We estimated each task's success probability once using the base policy before training and kept the selected training pool fixed throughout the run.
We used offline policy-relative difficulty to build the training pool, then fine-tuned Qwen3.8-27B with GRPO for 50 steps. To recap, we evaluate each of the 507 benchmark tasks 20 times. pass@1 measures average success across all 10,140 attempts. pass@20 measures the share of tasks solved at least once. Observed 20/20 measures the share of tasks that pass every recorded attempt.

items.excerpt:
Survey from IRU and Trimble shows that infrastructure has matured, but cost is now their biggest obstacle.
A survey of European logistics providers shows that road freight operators are continuing their efforts to cut emissions, but that their customers won’t pay the extra cost of greener transport.
The data showed that cost is now their biggest obstacle to going further, compared to last year’s survey, in which cost ranked second to infrastructure. Those numbers came from the “2026 Green Compact” survey conducted by world road transport organization group IRU and supply chain software provider Trimble.
That change has come because around seven in ten operators in Western Europe (70%), Eastern Europe (71%), and Australia (67%) say their customers are unwilling to pay the additional cost of decarbonization. That’s a problem because the price of decarbonizing is high, but operators have no reliable way to pass it on. Solutions are seen as too expensive by 64% of Western European operators, 62% in Eastern Europe and 40% in Australia.
Taken together, expensive solutions and unwilling customers form a “cost wall,” researchers said. The shift is clearest in alternative fuels. Last year, the lack of charging and refueling infrastructure was the leading obstacle. But in 2026, vehicle prices have become the biggest barrier in both European regions. In Western Europe, 66% of operators cite vehicle prices, up from 49% in 2025. In Eastern Europe, the figure has risen from 52% to 78%.
And indeed, the gap is large. An electric truck costs two to three times as much as its diesel equivalent, far more than operators’ thin margins can absorb, the study said.
Still, nine in ten Western European operators (90%) take at least one measure to cut emissions, as do 87% in Eastern Europe and 55% in Australia. They start with measures that pay for themselves: routing optimization (53% in Western Europe, 62% in Eastern Europe) and eco-driving training (42% in both).
